overview.description: Königrufen Lungau Tarock is a streamlined version of Austrian Tarock played in the Salzburger Lungau region. It features regular tournaments and simplified rules compared to traditional Königrufen. The reduced choice of contracts and simplified card counting lead to a sharper game where valuable cards are more important relative to empty cards.

history.origins: Developed in the Lungau region of Salzburg as a tournament-friendly variant of KÃ¶nigrufen. The streamlined rules were designed to make the game faster and more suitable for competitive play.
timeline: 19th Century: Traditional KÃ¶nigrufen played throughout Austria
Early 20th Century: Lungau variant develops with simplified rules
Present: One of the most competitive Tarock variants in Austria
history.evolution: The Lungau variant simplified the complex contract hierarchy of traditional KÃ¶nigrufen, reducing the number of available contracts and standardizing bonus values. The 'Fahren' (Trischaken) contract became the default when all players pass, adding tension to the bidding phase.
history.cultural: The Lungau region hosts prestigious Tarock tournaments. The game is considered a sharper, more tactical version of KÃ¶nigrufen due to the increased importance of high-value cards.

setup.players: Four active players. Five can participate with dealer sitting out each hand.
setup.deck: Standard Austrian 54-card Tarock pack: 22 trumps (Tarocks), 8 cards each in four suits.
setup.dealing: Dealer shuffles, player to left cuts. Deal 12 cards to each player in batches of 6, anticlockwise, starting with player to dealer's right. Place two packets of 3 cards face down in middle as talon.

rules.objective: Win tricks containing valuable cards. In positive contracts, need 36+ of 71 card points. Various contracts have different objectives.
rules.gameplay: Dealer deals 12 cards each and 6 to the talon. Players bid (Sechserdreier, Rufer mit Spatz/Uhu, Dreier) or say Erster; if all pass, Fahren is played. Bidder calls a King (in Rufer) or takes 3 or 6 talon cards and discards. Announcements and Kontras follow. Player to dealer's right leads; 12 tricks, follow suit, must trump if unable to follow. Highest trump wins trick, else highest of led suit. Team with 36+ of 71 card points wins the game; bonuses and game points are settled in cash.
keyRules: Deal 12 cards each and 6 to the talon in two packets of 3; deal and play anticlockwise.
Bid Sechserdreier, Rufer mit Spatz/Uhu, or Dreier, or say Erster; if all pass, Fahren is played.
In Rufer, call a King for partner; bidder takes 3 talon cards (or 6 in Sechserdreier) and discards; 5-point cards and most trumps cannot be discarded.
Follow suit; must trump if unable to follow. Highest Tarock wins trick, else highest of led suit. Player to dealer's right leads.
36+ of 71 card points wins the game; game points and bonuses (Trull, Four Kings, Pagat Ultimo, Uhu, King Ultimo, Valat) settled in cash.

strategy.basic: In positive contracts, aim for 36+ points. The 5-point cards (SkÃ¼s, XXI, I, Kings) are crucial - there are only 8 of them totaling 40 points. Queens (4 pts) and Knights (3 pts) are also valuable.
strategy.intermediate: Talon selection: Look for packets with kings or high trumps. In Rufer, if the called king is in the talon, you play alone - consider this risk when calling. In Fahren, try to take as few points as possible - even taking zero points is a valid strategy.
strategy.advanced: Announcement timing: Announcing Pagat Ultimo or Uhu doubles their value but commits you to a specific play. Only announce if you have strong position in trumps. In Sechserdreier, with all 6 talon cards, you have perfect information - use this advantage. The risk/reward (+2/-4) means you need a strong hand to bid Sechserdreier.
tips: Track the 22 trumps carefully - knowing which high trumps remain is essential.
In Rufer mit Spatz/Uhu, the announced bonus can be won/lost independently of the game.
Fahren is dangerous if you have many high cards - sometimes bidding a weak Rufer is safer.
The Uhu (trump II) is easier to make than Pagat Ultimo as it's played earlier.

difficulty.easy: Random talon selection. Poor bidding decisions. Doesn't track trumps.
difficulty.medium: Reasonable talon choice. Basic bidding thresholds. Tracks high trumps. Understands Fahren vs. Rufer decision.
difficulty.hard: Optimal bidding based on hand evaluation. Perfect card tracking. Calculates exact probabilities for bonuses. Masters the risk/reward of Sechserdreier.

trumpConfig.trumpSuitRanking: Sküs highest then XXI down to I (Pagat)
trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Highest Tarock in trick wins; if no Tarocks, highest card of led suit wins.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: Player to dealer's right leads first trick.

edgeCases.text: In Fahren (Trischaken) the talon is not used; each player must beat the highest card so far in the trick if possible; holder of Pagat cannot lead or play it until it is their only remaining Tarock.
5-point cards (Kings, Sküs, XXI, Pagat) cannot be discarded; trumps II–XX only if no alternative (hand would be all trumps and Kings); discarded trumps placed face up.
If called King is in talon in Rufer, bidder may take half talon and play alone or surrender (schleifen) for 3 game points to each opponent.

Announced Pagat Ultimo or Uhu fails if the card is beaten by a higher trump in the scheduled trick or not played to that trick; Uhu must be played before Pagat if both announced and one must be played early.

customActions.description: Place two packets of 3 cards face down in the middle of the table to form the talon (at start of deal or between the two rounds of 6 cards).
Say 'Erster' (first) to pass the bid without undertaking a contract; if first player says Erster and all others pass, a Fahren is played.
customActions.constraints: First player only in bidding; alternative to bidding a contract.

customActions.description: Name a King; the holder of that King is the bidder's partner (in Rufer). If the called King is in the talon or in the bidder's hand, bidder plays alone.
customActions.constraints: Bidder only after a Rufer bid; before talon exchange.

customActions.description: Take 3 or 6 cards from the talon (according to contract), add to hand, and discard same number face down. In Rufer/Dreier choose one 3-card packet; in Sechserdreier take all 6. 5-point cards and most trumps cannot be discarded.
customActions.constraints: Bidder only after bidding; discard rules restrict which cards may be discarded.

customActions.description: Announce a bonus (Trull, Four Kings, Pagat Ultimo, Uhu, King Ultimo, Valat) to double its score if made, or announce Kontra/Rekontra/Subkontra to double game or bonus scores.
customActions.constraints: In announcement round after discard; Spatz/Uhu/King Ultimo only by holder of the card.

customActions.description: Play a card of the suit that was led when possible.
customActions.constraints: Must follow suit if able; otherwise must play a Tarock if holding any.

customActions.description: Play a Tarock when unable to follow suit; must trump if you have no card of the led suit.
customActions.constraints: Only when unable to follow suit and holding at least one Tarock.

customActions.description: Add up the value of counting cards in tricks (and talon share) for your team; total is 71, 36+ wins the game.
Compute net game points from contract result and bonuses (won or lost); losers pay winners (e.g. stake per game point).
customActions.constraints: After counting points and checking bonuses.

engine.deckDescription: A 54-card Industrie und Glück tarock deck with 21 numbered trumps plus the Skus and 32 suit cards. Black suits keep King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack, 10, 9, 8, 7; red suits keep King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack, Ace, 2, 3, 4.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits are divided into black suits (Spades and Clubs) and red suits (Hearts and Diamonds), each with its own reduced pip sequence.
engine.rankDescription: Courts are King, Queen, Cavalier, and Jack. Black suits continue with 10, 9, 8, 7; red suits continue with Ace, 2, 3, 4. Trumps run from 1 to 21 plus the Skus.
engine.dealPattern: Two rounds of 6 cards each to each player anticlockwise from right of dealer; two packets of 3 cards face down in centre as talon.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: Players do not draw from stock during play; cards are dealt once and talon exchange is contract-specific.
notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: No general discard pile; bidder discards only after talon exchange in specific contracts.
notApplicableReasons.meldConfig: No melding; this is a trick-taking game with point counting.
notApplicableReasons.shedding: Goal is to win tricks and card points, not to empty the hand.
notApplicableReasons.roundConfig: No fixed round count; session ends by agreement or Sküs round.
notApplicableReasons.declarationMechanism: Bonus announcements are made in turn, not chips-in-fist.
notApplicableReasons.marketConfig: No market; talon is exchanged by bidder only.
notApplicableReasons.bankingConfig: Settled in cash per game point, no banker.
notApplicableReasons.specialCards: No wild or action cards; all cards have fixed point values.

scoring.description: Card points counted individually (not in groups). Total 71 points, need 36+ to win. Game points and bonuses calculated separately.
scoring.winCondition: Win majority of 71 card points (36 or more) in tricks; contract and bonuses determine game points paid between teams.

nullReasons.targetScore: No fixed target score; play by game rules.
nullReasons.cardValues: Card point values are defined in engine; scoring uses sum of trick points (71 total, 36+ wins).
